editorial:
Imagine being in a marriage where you and your spouse both secretly want the other person dead, but you are too scared of getting caught to actually do it. That is the hilarious setup here. You meet Paul and Blandine, a couple who absolutely hate each other but are stuck in a polite, cold war. The vibe is light and witty, feeling more like a funny play than a dark crime story. It is a clever game of cat and mouse where the characters are trying to outsmart one another without ever saying what they actually mean out loud.

What really makes this work is the irony of Paul visiting a lawyer to learn how to commit the perfect crime. The dialogue is snappy, and the way the plot circles back on itself will keep you smiling. While it is an older black-and-white film, the pacing feels quick and the acting is top-notch. If you enjoy smart comedies with a twist, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: In the end, Paul tries to use the lawyer's advice to kill Blandine, but his plan backfires completely. The movie wraps up with a funny twist where the roles flip, and the attempt on her life fails. Instead of getting away with murder, Paul ends up stuck in his miserable marriage. It turns out that trying to cheat the legal system is harder than it looks, and the couple remains locked in their funny, hateful battle.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves clever scripts and husband-and-wife rivalry.
similarMovies: The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie
